newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO parliamentarians condemn Belarus referendum.
newsitem.headline: NATO parliamentarians condemn Belarus referendum.

text.p: NATO parliamentarians on Thursday demanded the cancellation of a planned referendum in Belarus to strengthen President Alexander Lukashenko's powers and urged Western governments not to recognise the result.

The North Atlantic Assembly, grouping parliamentarians from 40 states including NATO's 16 nations, criticised in a resolution what it called Lukashenko's "tendency...to reduce the degree of freedom and democracy enjoyed by citizens of Belarus".

Lukashenko is locked in a power struggle over Sunday's planned referendum with the Belarussian constitutional court and parliament, which accuse him of seeking to establish a dictatorship in the former Soviet republic.

"The Assembly urges member governments and parliaments to condemn violations of the constitution and laws of Belarus... insist categorically on the cancellation of the referendum (and) refuse to recognise the results of the referendum should all the violations not be eliminated," the resolution said.

It also urged member nations to "express political and moral support to the Supreme Council (parliament) and the people of Belarus in their efforts to defend the constitution, democracy and human rights in the Republic of Belarus".

In a related development, the Council of Europe said in a statement on Thursday that the draft constitution proposed by Lukashenko in the referendum "falls short of democratic minimum standards and violates the principle of separation of powers".

The 40-nation Council, which promotes democracy and human rights across Europe, said its European Commission for Democracy through Law had adopted a negative assessment of the draft submitted by the president.

"The main thrust of the criticism is that it excessively reinforces the powers of the president at the detriment of the powers of all other bodies like parliament and the constitutional court," the Council statement said.
